links.outcome: Section segmentation performance drop from in-domain MIMIC-III to out-of-domain obstetrics notes
links.effect: Supervised models performed strongly in-domain but their performance dropped substantially out-of-domain; zero-shot LLMs adapted robustly once hallucinated section headers were corrected.
links.quote: Our results show that while supervised models perform strongly in-domain, their performance drops substantially out-of-domain.

unlisted_practices: Correcting hallucinated section headers in zero-shot LLM output before use
Curating domain-specific section-labeled clinical datasets (e.g., obstetrics) to supplement public corpora

screen.reason: Evaluates zero-shot LLMs against supervised transformer models for clinical section segmentation across MIMIC-III and a new obstetrics dataset, assessing out-of-domain transfer and noting hallucinations without evaluating a formal organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
